lesson_title: One Oven, Two Breads: the Production Possibility Curve
hook_text: One oven. Two breads. Every economics exam ever — in a bakery.
clip_script: A bakery: one oven, two bakers, one day. All white bread: 50 loaves. All brown: 50. Mix them — and here's the iron rule: every extra brown is PAID FOR in whites. The day is fixed; push one up, the other comes down. Draw the possible days as a line and you get a boundary — the edge of the possible. Now the three kinds of day. The FULL day: everything humming — that's ON the line, the maximum. The LAZY day: a baker off sick, the oven idle an hour — INSIDE the line. Nothing shrank; you just didn't use what you had. For a country, inside the line is where unemployment lives. The DREAM day — 50 whites AND 40 browns? BEYOND the line. Impossible... until the bakery buys a second oven, and the whole boundary steps outward. That's growth. And the sharpest lesson: a country with millions of idle hands doesn't need a new oven first. Its cheapest growth is walking back to the line — using what it already has.
visual_style: A warm dawn bakery: loaves stacking into a plotted curve, three days lighting up as points (on, inside, beyond); a second oven wheeling in as the boundary breathes outward; a final wide shot of hands returning to work.
mood: Cosy craft energy sharpening into national insight.
pacing: Steady kneading rhythm through the menu, three clean point-beats, expansive finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and read any economy's possibilities off one curve.
